we use a or an before one thing
Write "an" before a vowel sound; write "a" before other sounds.

Rule: I am / he, she, it is / you, we, they are.
Verbs ending in a consonant plus y change to -ies ... Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -s, -x or -o take -es.
Rule: after he, she or it, add -s or -es to the verb.
Right: She sells flowers. Wrong: She sell flowers.
in English we never leave out am, is or are
"He tired" is wrong; "He is tired" is right.
after he, she and it, we add -s to the verb
Rule: am for I; is for he, she, it; are for you, we, they.
"You are kind" is right. "You is kind" is wrong.
